title: heterogeneous-backpressure-stage-coordinator-for-latency-stability
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: implement a stage-level backpressure and crediting coordinator that harmonizes tensor- and pipeline-parallel stages to maximize NCCL overlap during prefill/decode waves while keeping tail latency under SLOs. Motivation: current prefill/decode interaction produces microbursts that either starve NCCL windows (reducing overlap) or create buffering spikes on devices (tail latency regression). The proposed coordinator uses per-stage credit tokens, stage fencing with adaptive rendezvous windows, and kernel-hinting signals to: 1) prioritize kernel choices that reduce staging time (e.g., favor fused attention kernels when sequence length < 1024 on A100/RTX-8000), 2) gate KV cache slot handoff to avoid head-of-line prefill spikes, and 3) compact communicative phases to increase NCCL concurrency. Scope: runtime change (inference conductor), no model architecture change. Components: credit manager, stage fence state machine, kernel-hint API for model loader, metrics/observability hooks. Success criteria: 10-25% increase in NCCL time overlap on heterogenous device pools for mixed prefill+decode workloads, <5% regression in median latency, <8% regression in p99 compared to baseline, and no increased OOM incidents across our test fleet.
comments: 2025-03-12 - Aisha Patel: Initial writeup and proposal. Added high-level sequence diagrams to Confluence (link below). Raised blockers: need kernel selection knobs surfaced from compilation layer.

2025-03-13 - Liam O'Connor: Prototype credit manager implemented locally. Early microbench shows smoother token arrival but NCCL overlap did not increase — hypothesize we need rendezvous coalescing (batching small comms) in addition to backpressure.

2025-03-14 - Carlos Mendez (review): Reviewed stage fence design. Suggest consolidating fence states into three explicit phases (Draining, Rendezvous, Release) to simplify proofs about deadlock freedom. Also requested concrete fallbacks for straggler stages (spill-to-host or local-queue bypass).

2025-03-15 - QA: Perf run 2025-03-15 attached. Notes: on heterogeneous cluster (2xA100 + 1xRTX8000) mixed workload, median latency unchanged, p99 improved by 6% for decode-heavy traces, but NCCL overlap increased only 4% in this run. Need further kernel-hint integration.

2025-03-16 - Research: Ran kernel-selection matrix across sequence lengths [128,512,1024,2048] on devices. Observed that attention fusion reduces per-token compute by 12-18% up to seq=1024 but regresses memory footprint at 2048 on RTX8000. Decided to make kernel hints conditional on seq_len and device micro-arch.

2025-03-17 - Ops: Noted a reproducible hung trace when a stage reported a negative credit count due to double-release from a timeout path. Added guarded release and metric for negative-credit events. Re-ran smoke tests — clean.

2025-03-18 - Liam O'Connor: Added adaptive rendezvous window. Early test: NCCL overlap +13% on synthetics when rendezvous window coalesces comms up to 4ms; p99 +3%. Next: add kernel hinting RPC and toggle in canary.

2025-03-18 - PM review (Janelle Ruiz): Prioritize rollout gating: must be disabled by default on dedicated nodes until we validate OOM/tail-latency across 5 customers. Add feature flag and telemetry events for rollout decisions.
next_steps: 1) Merge credit manager + guarded release to canary branch. 2) Implement kernel-hint RPC inside model loader and expose sequence-length/device hints. 3) Run canary across 10 dedicated nodes with mixed customer traces. 4) Collect telemetry for negative-credit events, NCCL overlap, p50/p99 latencies, and OOM occurrences. 5) Decide rollout by 2025-04-01.
notes: Trade-offs considered: aggressive coalescing increases NCCL overlap but can amplify tail latency if a straggler stage stalls; mitigations include bounded rendezvous window and spill-to-host bypass. We prefer correctness and SLA stability over maximal overlap. Implementation language: Rust (existing conductor codebase). Will require small changes to C++ kernel hint layer (compiler interface) — coordinate with infra-compiler team.
